subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native OpenClaw trust/provenance model should govern durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, Active Memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent fix requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, persisted schema/migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and native-versus-external integration boundaries.

options.title: Design native trust contract
options.body: Create a first-class memory trust/provenance contract owned by the host/runtime, then wire schema, retrieval, review, expiration, and plugin/MCP exposure to that contract.

options.title: Split provenance foundation first
options.body: Use #42647 and #48519 to land durable source provenance before adding trust tiers, review gates, and retrieval influence policy.

options.title: Defer to external integrations
options.body: Document external MCP/plugin trust systems as optional and leave OpenClaw native memory without enforced trust policy for now.

recommendation.title: Design native trust contract
recommendation.body: Create a first-class memory trust/provenance contract owned by the host/runtime, then wire schema, retrieval, review, expiration, and plugin/MCP exposure to that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main memory seam signal and participated in related maintainer review context.
